messages:
Eli: hey everyone :wave: quick follow-up from today's all-hands — leadership is here for an open Q&A on strategy, mission, and how we win vs bigger clouds. ask anything, we'll answer live.
Maya: happy to start — we want to be the predictable inference layer. not just model access, but predictable latency/cost/ops. that's our north star. :compass: 
Jordan: one clarifier: when we say 'unified runtime' we mean same API and rollout primitives across hosted, dedicated, and private — customers shouldn't have to rewire.
Liz: on roadmap: next 18mo focus is (1) Dedicated autoscaling improvements, (2) Private deployment UX, and (3) Optimize's recommendation engine. timing: staggered launches, not all at once.
Nick: question — customers keep asking: do we plan to develop our own models or lean entirely on open model ecosystem? curious tradeoffs.
Eli: short answer: we partner with open models and optimize serving for them. we may train targeted small models for specific features where it makes sense, but our moat is serving.
Maya: technical nuance: we care about model variants we can serve efficiently (quantized, kernel-friendly). model ownership is expensive; serving-by-default is higher leverage for our customers.
Oliver: Ops question from infra crew — SLAs for Dedicated: are we moving to 99.9% availability, and will there be credits or failover policies?
Jordan: yes, roadmap includes 99.9% SLA for Dedicated next year plus documented fallback policies. we'll also publish recommended routing policies for multi-region customers.
Amy: for GTM — should growth teams lean into 'cost predictability' vs 'model quality' messaging? which resonates most with prospects?
Eli: both, but lead with concrete numbers: "lower inference cost by X%", "SLO-backed latency". engineers buy on predictability; execs buy on unit economics.
Priya: follow-up: any changes to free tier or trial that we should know? converting free users to Dedicated is a big lever.
Jordan: we're testing a new trial flow that surfaces cost/perf dashboards during the trial so teams see the value. no global changes yet.
Nick: competitor angle — how do we position vs public cloud AI endpoints that bundle models and infra?
Maya: emphasize production controls: fine-grained routing, prefix caching, KV reuse, and rollback policies. clouds sell endpoints, we sell predictable inference at scale.
Liz: also call out observability — token-level cost and per-route latency dashboards are unique and very tactical for platform teams.
Oliver: ops note: make sure SRE runbooks are public to customers for Private installs. customers ask for that during procurement.
Eli: agreed. we'll make runbooks and an onboarding checklist standard for enterprise deals.
Amy: sales ask — are we increasing pricing transparency for Dedicated/reserved plans? reps need clear 3-tier pricing to share with prospects.
Jordan: pricing review is in motion. aim is clearer bands (small/medium/large commitments) and a cost-savings calculator for reps.
Priya: product question — will Optimize automatically suggest quantization profiles or just recommendations?
Maya: Optimize will start with suggestions and diagnostics; later we plan automated safe-recommendations with opt-out.
Nick: tiny engineering ask — can we get a canonical benchmark doc to share externally (latency/cost comparisons vs open cloud endpoints)?
Liz: yes, marketing+eng are collaborating on a reproducible benchmark repo and a short playbook for customer conversations.
AllHandsBot: poll: "Which 18mo outcome matters most to you?" options: 1) Dedicated SLA & scale 2) Private onboardings 3) Optimize automation 4) Observability wins. react with 1/2/3/4.
Eli: last note — keep sending questions here, we'll follow up with an FAQ doc after we synthesize. thanks for the great questions! :rocket: 
Amy: thanks leadership — I'll surface the benchmark ask to sales enablement and get a kickoff.
Nick: appreciate the clarity, especially on serving-first stance. helps prioritize infra work.
Oliver: will start drafting customer-facing runbook checklist.
Jordan: we'll share timeline snapshots in #product-weekly once we have nitty-gritty dates.
Priya: recording + short FAQ expected by end of week.
Eli: excellent — closing thread for now but keep threads coming. :slightly_smiling_face:
